FOR AGENTS

Customer information: a new tab beside Customer on the call screen keeps a customer's numbers, emails, physical and postal addresses, preferred way and time to be contacted, notes and your organisation's own fields. On a dialler call it is filled from the campaign list's columns, marked "from the list" until you save. If a colleague saved the same customer meanwhile, you are told who and when, and what you typed is kept. Required fields are highlighted but never stop you saving or finishing wrap-up.

Screens that keep up by themselves: the desk, Floor, live monitor and wallboards now change the moment something happens, instead of asking the platform every few seconds. After a restart, screens reconnect gently rather than all at once.

Your connection: a dot in the top bar shows whether your connection is good, fair or poor, with the figures behind it. Test my connection checks your network, the phone and your microphone in about ten seconds and says in plain words what to do.

One desk per sign-in: you can be signed in to the desk in one place at a time. Signing in somewhere else takes over and the old desk says "Signed in on another device"; a call still running there carries on until it ends.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS AND SUPERVISORS

Customer information forms: choose which fields each customer group sees and which are required, map a lead list's columns to the customer's details (Auto-map does most of it), and fill existing leads after a preview. When an import would change details agents have saved, you choose whether to overwrite them or keep the agents' values.

Agents' connections: the Floor flags agents whose connection is fair or poor, an agent's sheet shows the last 24 hours, every call keeps its quality figures including the worst ten seconds, and a new report, Call quality by agent, shows patterns by agent or site. An optional alert tells team leaders when an agent's connection stays poor.

Sign-in rules: choose whether a second sign-in takes over (the default) or is refused, and how many console sessions supervisors may keep. Supervisors can sign an agent out remotely from the Floor or Users; on a call it asks first and ends the call only when you say so. A Shared sign-ins report and an optional alert show logins that keep being taken over from different places.

FOR PLATFORM OPERATORS

Availability: Platform → Servers has an Availability tab. It estimates the uptime of each service from the servers you actually run and names the weakest link, measures the real uptime over 7, 30 and 90 days with planned work kept apart, gives each client a monthly SLA report against its contract, and plans what it takes to reach a target, from 99.9% to 99.999%.

Protection levels: Platform → Servers shows four levels side by side: Standard, Resilient, Full HA with a spare site, and Ultra HA (two live sites in one metro region, about 99.998%), with where this platform stands and a checklist for the next level. Ultra HA's multi-site parts are planned and marked so."}
